title: Building and Maintaining Rapport Within a Telehealth Service Delivery Model
abstract: ABSTRACT Building and maintaining rapport throughout service delivery is vital to the therapeutic relationship between clinicians and staff/caregivers. During service delivery, effective communication and positive interactions may produce sustainable changes that benefit the staff/caregiver and the client as well as programmatic outcomes. A systematic review of 55 studies spanning the past decade of ABA telehealth research was conducted and not a single article operationalized rapport‐building as a trainable clinician skill, leaving a gap between the field's reliance on rapport and its guidance for building it. This paper addresses that gap by outlining effective interpersonal therapeutic skills based on an active listening model. This model has been identified as an effective tool and may be particularly beneficial in ABA‐based service delivery, given telehealth's decade‐long presence in ABA service delivery. The target responses involved in the active listening model include both verbal and non‐verbal behavior, therefore, we analyzed target clinician responses in accordance with Skinner's analysis of verbal behavior, including the use of echoics and intraverbals. A task analysis and fidelity checklist were created to ensure clinicians acquire and incorporate these skills during a therapeutic session.
